chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Karkhi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who arrived in Mecca with his sacrificial animal (hady) during the ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is an obligatory sacrifice, he should not slaughter it except in Mina; and if it is not obligatory, let him slaughter it in Mecca if he wishes; and if he had already marked it or adorned it, he should not slaughter it except on the Day of Eid al-Adha.'

key_terms.الْعَشْرِ: The ten days of Dhu al-Hijj
key_terms.هَدْي: Sacrificial animal brought by a pilgrim for Hajj

ai.seo_question: Where and when should a pilgrim slaughter their sacrificial animal during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the juristic distinction between obligatory (*wajib*) and voluntary (*nafl*) sacrifices, emphasizing that the location of slaughter is tied to the legal status of the vow rather than mere preference. It further refines the ruling by noting that once an animal is consecrated (*ahram* or *qallad*), it must be slaughtered specifically on the Day of Eid al-Adha (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah), reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise adherence to the temporal and spatial markers of Hajj rituals.
